summary:
We developed a lunar base management simulator based on NASA’s Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) architecture. Our project addresses the challenge of making aerospace engineering engaging by bridging the gap between rigorous scientific data and interactive learning.

The simulator uses a cause-and-effect "System-of-Systems" interface where subsystems like oxygen filtration, energy grids, hydroponics, and radiation shielding are highly interconnected. Players must balance these limited resources; for instance, diverting power to the greenhouse might cause the air purifier to fail.

This project matters because it makes space engineering accessible. By having players manage critical resources under pressure, the game teaches practical problem-solving. It shows the next generation the real challenges of deep-space survival without relying on complex math.
details:
What it does and how it works

Lunar Outpost is a lunar base management simulator grounded in NASA’s Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS). Players manage critical resources—oxygen, energy, radiation shielding, and food. It operates on a visual "System-of-Systems" model where every action triggers a direct consequence (e.g., diverting power to the greenhouse shuts down the oxygen purifiers). The game also integrates NASA's DONKI API to trigger real space weather events.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project transforms complex aerospace engineering into an accessible, interactive experience. By removing mathematical barriers and focusing on visual problem-solving, it teaches genuine systems thinking. Our ultimate goal is to inspire youth (ages 7-12) to pursue STEM fields by letting them experience the true logistical challenges of deep-space survival.

  • Tools and Technologies
  • Core Development: Python and Pygame.
  • Data Integration: NASA DONKI API.
  • Media & Design: Custom pixel art, MP4 cinematic backgrounds, and multimedia editors.
  • Workflow: Visual Studio Code, Git, and GitHub.
  • Hardware: Runs efficiently on standard PCs with no specialized hardware or constant internet required.

How it is creative Instead of relying on typical sci-fi combat, we gamified extreme logistics. It blends approachable, nostalgic pixel art with cinematic video backgrounds, transforming abstract scientific data into a high-pressure, highly entertaining survival experience.

 

Key factors considered

  • Scientific Integrity: We strictly separate real NASA data from in-game randomized events to ensure accurate learning without scientific distortion.
  • Cognitive Load: The 100% visual interface prevents information overload, allowing young players to grasp complex engineering concepts intuitively.
  • Socioeconomic Reach: The simulator operates completely offline. This bridges the digital divide, ensuring any school can use this STEM tool regardless of internet infrastructure.
